3.      PUBLIC HEARINGS


        a)   BYLAW NO. 1767
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 527, (2668, 2674, 2682, 2684, 2686, 2696 2702
             & 2706 Sooke Rd), 2018".


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1767 at 5:31 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                                   April 16th, 2018
                                                                                                       Page 2 of 8



The City Planner advised that Niall Paltiel of Keycorp Planning Ltd. has applied on behalf of Oakcrest Park
Estates to amend the zoning of 2668, 2674, 2682, 2684, 2686, 2696, 2702 & 2706 Sooke Rd from the C3
(District Commercial) and CS1 (Service Commercial) Zone to a new C9 (Community Town Centre
Pedestrian 9) Zone.


This is being proposed in order to allow a mixed-used development that may include high density
residential as well as commercial uses.


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following contributions per
residential unit, prior to issuance of a building permit, as a bonus for increased density:

      i. $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund, and
      ii. $2,074 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund, for which Council may use this towards the
          construction of the realignment of Glen Lake Road and DCC works on Sooke Road.


The applicant has also agreed to provide a technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can
be adequately managed for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering,
prior to public hearing — which they have.

Additionally, prior to Bylaw Adoption, the applicant will provide a Section 219 covenant that agrees to the
following:

       i. That the owner will not apply for, nor is the City obligated to issue a Development Permit or
          Building Permit until road dedication is provided to the satisfaction of the Director of
          Engineering and Approving Officer.

       ii. That at any time after the 5 th anniversary date of adoption of the bylaw to rezone the subject
           lands, the City may request, and the owner shall provide, the area of land necessary for the
           construction of the road extension from Happy Valley Road to Glen Lake Road as well as Sooke
           Road for $1.00.

      iii. That the owner will limit direct vehicular access to Sooke Road, and will not apply for, nor will
           the City be obligated to grant driveway access on to Sooke Road, except in accordance with a
           comprehensive plan of development for the properties as a whole.

      iv. That a Traffic Impact Assessment be completed to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering
          for the full build-out of any block that commercial and/or residential uses are proposed on, prior
          to the issuance of building permit, and that the recommendations of the Traffic Impact
             Assessment be implemented prior to occupancy of any building;

       v. That all frontage improvements to Bylaw 1000 standards are provided to the satisfaction of the
          Director of Engineering and Manager of Parks prior to issuance of a building permit; and

      vi. That a detailed storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building permit
          and implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

                                                                                                   April 16th, 2018
                                                                                                       Page 3 of 8



This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood and Neighbourhood Centre
designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.


The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Resident on Anders Road addressed Council wondering of there was an easement, as red ribbons showed
up 10 days ago.

Michelle Mahovlich, Director of Engineering provided a response.


Resident on Page Road expressed concern over height of the building and minimal size of setbacks. Also
wondered if change was because of inclusion of hotel lands.

Mathew Baldwin, Director of Planning provided a response and clarification.

Resident on Anders Road asked about density.


Mayor Young provided clarification (depends on stormwater and parking).

Resident asked about the realignment of Glen Lake road and about sound-deadening fencing.


Mayor Young provided clarification.

Resident on Anders Road is curious about setbacks and sound deadening fence.


Mathew Baldwin, Director of Planning provided clarification.

Resident on Anders Road asked about setbacks from the galloping goose trail.


Resident on Wilshire Drive asked about left hand turn from Sooke onto Wilshire.


Mayor Young and Michelle Mahovlich, Director of Engineering provided clarification and that traffic would
be directed through a signalized intersection.

Jim Hartshorne answered all questions.
    -   Ribbons — in realtion to a storm drain issue
    -   Fencing — 6 feet
    -   Density/Site coverage — less than the allowable 70%
    -  Sound deadening fence — definitely putting something idown Anders road
    -  Traffic — will improve Sooke Road in conjunction with Ministry of Transportation and
         Infrastructure and understood through traffic study


Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

None presented.

                                                                                                     April 16th, 2018
                                                                                                          Page 4 of 8




The Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Mayor officially declared
the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1767 closed at 5:52 p.m.
